intended_object: The fibre functor of the Galois category of finite covering spaces of X: it sends a finite covering p : E → X to its fibre p⁻¹(x₀), a finite set, and a map of covers to its restriction to fibres (SGA1 Exp. V; module docstring and the docstring).
explanation:
The body composes the library's equivalence between finite covering spaces of X and Mathlib's finite π₁(X, x₀)-sets (`Action FintypeCat`) with the functor that forgets the action. That equivalence is built from the fibre-action functor, which sends a cover to its fibre over x₀ with the monodromy action. So the composite sends a cover to its fibre over x₀ as a finite set. The library proves this with `fiberFunctor_obj`: the underlying type is `p.proj ⁻¹' {x₀}`. On morphisms it is restriction to fibres, which is `fiberFunctor_map_hom`. This is the standard fibre functor.

The hypotheses (path connected, locally path connected, semilocally simply connected) come from building the functor through the classification equivalence. The comment says this route was chosen so that the transported actions hold definitionally. The bare fibre functor p ↦ p⁻¹(x₀) would make sense over any base. But the object meant here is the fibre functor of the Galois category of finite covers, and those hypotheses are exactly the ones under which that structure, and the library's `FiberFunctor` instance, exist. I don't count this as genuinely too narrow. Mathlib has the abstract `PreGaloisCategory.FiberFunctor` class but no fibre functor for covering spaces.
